assertions.name: u_has_double_zero_at_q1
assertions.source: ℏ_q linear in t ⇒ ℏ_q² (hence u=b·ℏ_q²) vanishes to order 2 at q=1, b-independent. Scalar t(u) reversion therefore singular.

assertions.name: b_nonzero_at_anchor
assertions.source: Hoefsmit b(q_0)≈0.8676 ≠ 0 (N3 witness) ⇒ the double zero of u is real, not an accidental b-cancellation.

assertions.name: scalar_reversion_singular
assertions.source: ord_t(u)=2 ∧ ℏ_q'(0)≠0 ∧ u'(0)=0 ∧ b≠0 ⇒ scalar-q c_k series singular; c_k must be operator-level (Hoefsmit T_β chain).

description: Formalize-first foundation for the Q_β c_k operator-valued derivation tranche. ℏ_q=(q−1)/q is linear in t=q−1, so u=b·ℏ_q² has a b-INDEPENDENT double zero at q=1 (u=b(1)t²+O(t³)); the reversion t(u) needs a u^{1/2} branch, so R=∏(1+c_k u^k) is a clean integer-power u-series only if R is even in t (bar-even). α_EM's [2]_q·(1−h²α) is bar-even (scalar route worked); the Q_β trace-difference is not bar-fixed archimedean, so the scalar c_k series is singular. ⇒ the c_k are OPERATOR-LEVEL (N=k) coefficients of the Hoefsmit T_β chain (each level→u^k by substrate scaling), not scalar Taylor coefficients. This prunes the scalar class (refuted C1..C12) and motivates the operator route (keystone recipe Stages 1–5; first gate N=2→c_2=−1). No fit, no extraction. Diagnostic-only.
